findings.reason: without a per-model time_budget key added to §1's schema, the §3 node either loses the 40-minute budget (regressing the retired block's behaviour) or discovers mid-build that its declared write paths cannot express the change.
findings.text: §3 retires claude-opus by turning its one real difference, the 40-minute time budget, into "a per-model override on opus", but §1 (line 43) declares the per-model key set as only model, effort, alias, rates/as_of and budget_group — time_budget is listed among the LANE-level keys, so the schema §1 builds has no home for a per-model budget and §3 cannot preserve opus's 40m against the lane's 25m

findings.reason: §3 and §6 both assert "resolved flight unchanged" as their headline measure, which is exactly the assertion a no-op satisfies, so without a declared control (or a positive assertion that the blocks were actually collapsed — §3 has one, §6 has none) the gate cannot distinguish a completed fold from an untouched tree.
findings.text: §6's done-when is the identity check (resolved flight identical for all 14 projects) plus a dry-run equivalence, and names no negative control; a worker that makes no edit passes the identity check outright, and §3 and §7 likewise declare no control that shows their guard fires

findings.reason: the node must resolve the population it proves over; a hardcoded count that has already drifted leaves a project unverified (or blocks the node on a mismatch), and it is the same fuse the repo's own test-visibility rule warns against — derive the count at measure time rather than writing it down.
findings.text: the no-value-moves measure for §1, §3 and §6 is stated as "all 14 mounted projects", but ~/.config/reckon/mounts.json carries 15 project mounts, so the literal is a moving count written into the measure's population

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited report, the design run r-20261007T043246695894, revision 65d0bf6e7, and the write paths (reckon/_flight_schema.py, reckon/flight.py, reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py, docs/state/reckon/model-catalogue.yaml) all resolve; one-typesafe-model-picker#s6 resolves with the house .html extension.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3, §6 and §7 name no negative control, and §6's only structural check (resolved flight identical) passes on a no-op.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the cited artifact (the design report at ~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/lane-and-model-design/report.md) is on a durable path, and no section names a session scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test and symbol names (test_flight_lanes.py, test_dispatch_names_a_model.py, test_old_names_resolve.py) are mechanism-named, with no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3's mechanism depends on a per-model time_budget key that §1's schema does not declare, and the measure's population "14 mounted projects" is a hardcoded count that no longer matches the mounted set.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §1–§7 names one deliverable (schema, catalogue, host-flight collapse, dispatch flag, picker pairs, codex fold, resolver).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan's only cross-plan dependency, §5's hold on the picker's prompt work, is declared as gate g-lmr-1 gating s5 with required evidence one-typesafe-model-picker#s6, and that anchor resolves correctly (the jev-prompt run's own evidence fragment declares plan-verifies reckon:one-typesafe-model-picker#s6).
